/gully-id: Gully ID: the Gully Labs sign-in service · Gully Labs
Gully ID (gullyid.xyz) is the sign-in and wallet service built and run by Gully Labs: one passkey for every Gully app, never a seed phrase or a key.
/about: Gully Labs is a blockchain development company that designs, builds and releases Web3 products under its own name, and builds for other teams too.
/products/gully-id: Passwordless sign-in for any app: passkeys, wallets and email over OpenID Connect, with per-app consent. Live charts on this page.
/products/chain: An Arbitrum Orbit L3 for launches and trading, with Gully Core built in as its launchpad and DEX core. Live charts on this page.
/products/street: The Gully Chain app: a social feed, five wallets per passkey, copy trading, Quests and the launchpad. Live charts on this page.
/products/bridge: Move ETH between Arbitrum Sepolia and Gully Chain: a Hyperlane fast lane (gETH) and the canonical bridge. Live charts on this page.
/products/safe: Multisig wallets on Gully Chain, for treasuries and teams. Live charts, features, how it works, pricing and FAQ for Gully Multisig on this page.
/products/gully-sentry: Free testnet Sentry Keys and light watchers that check every Gully Chain assertion against their own node. Live charts on this page.
/products/pay: x402 payments, hosted checkout and a merchant OS, settled on chain to your own wallet. Live charts, features, pricing and FAQ on this page.
/products/rpc: One key for every network: the node control plane and RPC gateway behind every Gully chain. Live charts, features, pricing and FAQ on this page.
/products/holders: Who really holds a token: bubble maps, wallet clusters and deep checks, Gully Chain tokens included. Live charts on this page.
/products/security: AI security scans, contract monitors and the Gully Score for any contract, Gully Chain contracts included. Live charts on this page.
/products/ai: Answers about Gully with sources and live figures; the Gully AI API opens when its GPU box is up. Live charts on this page.
/products/studio: Our game studio: Unity 3D titles on Gully Chain with the Gully Game SDK, paid through Gully Pay. Live charts on this page.
/products/ipfs: Our IPFS node and read-only gateway for Gully content: token art, metadata, NFT art and .gully sites. Live charts on this page.
/products/quests: On-chain quests on Gully Chain: tasks verified by contract, rewards paid from ETH pools. Live charts, features, pricing and FAQ on this page.
/products/offerwall: Advertisers fund quests through Gully Pay; players complete them on Gully Chain and earn USDC or points; publishers embed the wall and earn a share.
/products/gully-social: The social layer of Gully Chain: posts, follows, replies and profiles tied to your wallet and .gully name, in the kre8.fun app. Live charts on this page.
/products/copy-trading: Follow a Gully Chain trader and mirror their trades from your own passkey wallet, with your own limits and an on-chain fee capped at 1%.
/products/gully-core: Gully Chain’s own launchpad and DEX core: a token and its pool in one step, graduating to Gully Swap. Live charts on this page.
/projects/peddleswap: PeddleSwap is a Gully Labs project (DEX). Swap. Lock. Launch. Swap tokens, earn fees from liquidity, lock tokens or LP and bridge networks.
/projects/peddles: Peddles is a Gully Labs project (Launchpad). Launch, trade and play. Memecoins paired to tokenised stocks. Holders are paid in that stock.
/projects/peddlequest: PeddleQuest is a Gully Labs project (Quest to earn). Verified quests on four chains. XP, soulbound badges, reward pools escrowed first.

Questions or requests about your data:.

Identity and access: signing in with your wallet. The app signs you in with Sign-In with Ethereum: you sign a message, and no password or email is needed. We keep your wallet address, when you first and last signed in, and whether the account is blocked. Each sign-in creates a session that stores a hash of a random session id (never the id itself), when it was created, last used and expires, your browser’s user agent and which workspace you have open. We don’t store your IP address with your account or sessions.

Workspaces and teams. A workspace’s name, its members’ wallet addresses and roles, who invited whom and when, and invites (an invite link is kept only as a hash). If you add them: a display name, an email address, notification choices, and company details (name, postal address, tax ID) for invoices. To show your ENS or Basename we look your address up through public Ethereum and Base nodes and keep the answer for 24 hours. An activity log records who changed what in the workspace (for example a key created or a plan paid), without IP addresses.

API keys and usage. We keep a hash of each key (never the key itself), its prefix and name, and count requests per key: per hour by result and endpoint, per day, and the last 50 requests (time, method, path, status and response time). Anonymous requests are limited per IP address in memory only; we don’t store those IPs.

Voluntary correspondence: contact and waitlists. When you write to us through the contact form: your name, email, message, the kind of project and budget you pick. When you join the Gully Chains waitlist: the contact you give (an email or a Telegram @username), your project’s name, the answers you choose and any notes. The Chain Kit and devnet waitlists in the app keep your email, your wallet and workspace, and for Chain Kit the chain you name. A project or launchpad submitted for the ecosystem page keeps its website, contact, chains, factory address and note.

Each of these also goes to our operators’ Telegram chat as a short message with the details, and once a day the chat gets a count of what is new. Operators can export the lists as CSV files. If the contact you give is a Telegram @username and that account has started @GullyLabsBot, the bot sends you one short thank-you. Our server sends no email.

Chains you launch. The app’s chain launch flow (testnet only) keeps the chain’s name, chain id, type and gas token, its owner, validator and batch-poster addresses, the deployment transaction and contract addresses, and which wallet recorded it. It never receives a private key or seed phrase and refuses any request that looks like one.

Gully Analytics is our own, self-hosted fork of the open-source Umami analytics, at analytics.gullylabs.xyz. Its script loads on gullylabs.xyz, docs.gullylabs.xyz, app.gullylabs.xyz, blog.gullylabs.xyz and holdermaps.xyz. Customers can use it on their own sites too. We don’t load any other analytics or advertising script.
It sets no cookies. A visit is grouped by a hash of the site, your IP address, your browser and a salt that changes every month, so we can’t follow you from month to month.

Your IP address is used to work out your country, region and city and is then dropped; it isn’t stored. We also record the page, referrer, browser, operating system, device type, screen size and language.
The checkout pages (pay.gullylabs.xyz) and the widgets and frames (embed.gullylabs.xyz) load no analytics at all.

In the app, where you connect a wallet, it records wallet connects and disconnects, chain switches and transactions you send, with the chain and wallet type. By default the wallet address is stored only as a short hash (the first 16 characters of its SHA-256). That is pseudonymous, not anonymous: anyone who knows your address can compute the same hash.
To opt out in a browser, set the local storage value umami.disabled to 1 for the site.
Geolocation. Cloudflare, which carries our traffic, tells our server the country of each request. We use it only to decide whether the stock token swap may be shown, and don’t store it.
If you sign up for Gully Analytics, we also keep your wallet address, your sites, your plan and trial dates, and monthly event counts. Your Umami password is never stored by us.

Server logs. Our own server keeps no log of every request. It logs errors and service events, which can include the address of a page or API call, and our network edge (Cloudflare and the proxy in front of our server) can log requests, including IP addresses, to keep the services secure. We keep these logs only as long as we need them to run and secure the services, then delete them.

When you ask Gully AI a question (on the site, in the app or with /ask in Telegram), we log the question, how long the answer was (not the answer itself), which sources and live tools it used, whether you were signed in, and a salted hash of your IP address, or of your Telegram chat id. If you rate an answer with a thumbs up or down, we keep the rating with the question and the same hash, so we know which docs to write. We keep questions and ratings for 90 days.

To write the answer, the question, your last few messages in that conversation and the matching passages of our docs are sent to Anthropic (Claude). When semantic search is switched on, the question is also sent to Voyage AI to compare it with our docs. When you are signed in to the app (or ask in a private Telegram chat linked to your wallet), Gully AI can read your own workspace’s store, API usage and alerts to answer, read-only; it never sees another workspace. The app also remembers your recent questions in your own browser.

Using @GullyLabsBot requires following the Gully Labs News channel; the bot checks this with Telegram and remembers the answer for up to 30 minutes, in memory only. If you link a chat to your wallet for alerts, we keep the chat id and type, the chat’s title (for a private chat, your first and last name and @username as Telegram gives them), your Telegram user id and when you linked it. Link codes are kept only as hashes and expire after 10 minutes. You can unlink at any time with /stop or in the bot’s settings.

Bot records. For every chat that uses the bot we keep when it was first and last seen, its language, your Telegram @username (lower-cased, so a thank-you can reach you when you give it on a form), whether it is linked to a wallet, whether it follows the News channel, whether it has blocked the bot or switched announcements off, and how it found the bot. No other names and no message text are kept in these records.

Writing to the team (/contact). When you write to us through the bot, each message (and any photo or file with it) is passed on to our operators’ Telegram chat with your name, @username and Telegram user id, and our replies come back through the bot. The text is not stored on our server: it stays in the two Telegram chats. Our server keeps only which operator message belongs to which chat (the newest 5,000, for 30 days), whether a conversation is open (it closes after 24 hours without messages) and the user ids we stopped relaying for.

Inline lookups. When you type “@GullyLabsBot” and a token in any chat, the token is looked up like any Holder Map lookup; your Telegram user id is used only to limit lookups per minute, in memory. Launch radar posts in the News channel are built from Holder Maps we already made, which are public chain data.

Announcements. The bot sometimes sends news to chats chosen by those records (for example linked chats, chats with alerts, followers of the News channel, a language, or chats active recently). For each announcement we keep, per recipient chat, whether it was delivered (with Telegram’s message id or error). Its buttons go through a link made for that recipient, so when you open one we record that this recipient opened it, once; we don’t record when, your IP address or your browser. Every announcement has a 🔕 Stop announcements button, and Settings switches them off and on again; that never affects your alerts.
The Mini App checks Telegram’s signed launch data to know who you are and stores nothing: no cookie and no session.

Scans. When your workspace runs an AI Security Scan we keep a record of it: the workspace, the wallet that started it, when, what was scanned (a contract address and chain, a GitHub repository and commit, or an uploaded file’s name and size), its price or invoice and its status. To run the scan we store the code on our server: the file you upload, the full text of the source files fetched from the chain’s explorer or GitHub or unpacked from your upload, the tools’ output, the AI’s findings and the report. For a web2 scan, files named.env are stored with the rest of the code but are never sent to the AI or the scanning tools. Please don’t upload secrets.

Who sees it. Members of your workspace see its scans and reports; developers, admins and owners can start and cancel them. Gully Labs operators can see the list of scans (who started one, the target and its status). To review the code, the files in scope are sent to Anthropic (Claude) after common secret patterns (API keys, private-key blocks and similar) are replaced; that check works by pattern and can miss a secret. The contract address and chain are sent to Etherscan, Blockscout or Sourcify to fetch verified source, the repository and commit to GitHub, and for web2 scans the dependency list in package-lock.json to the npm registry.

Publishing. A workspace owner or admin can publish a finished report. It then becomes public: the target, the findings, file paths with their hashes, and any code comments the scan flagged as attempts to instruct the AI; draft proof-of-concept code and the workspace are left out. Search engines are asked not to index it unless the publisher allows it. Published reports count towards that contract’s Gully Score. Unpublishing takes the report off the site at once; the copy stays on our server, not shown.

Security Review requests. When you ask for a quote we keep what you send (name, email, project, scope, repository, contract, company, timeline) and the signed-in wallet if there is one. The request also goes to our admin inbox and to our operators’ Telegram chat. Requests are limited per IP address and email in memory only; the IP is not stored.

Monitors. For each contract your workspace watches we keep the contract, chain and name, your alert thresholds, your webhook address and its signing secret, whether Telegram is on, whether the contract may be listed publicly, the contract’s last read state, its last 100 events and the last 50 alert deliveries. The contract is read through public blockchain nodes. A monitor whose listing is on adds its events to that contract’s public Gully Score; with listing off, nothing the monitor records reaches the public.

Holder Map. Looking up a map needs no account. To show the maps opened most today we count one view per visitor per token per day, using a hash of the IP address made with a random key that is held in memory only and replaced every day; the counts are reset each UTC day. New maps are limited per IP address for a minute, in memory only. To build a map we send the token’s address (never anything about you) to public blockchain nodes (including dRPC and Gully Chain’s own nodes), Blockscout, Moralis, Solana nodes and the launchpad APIs we read launches from. Holder alerts are kept like other alerts, until you delete them.

Deep checks. For a Deep check we keep the chain and token, its price, its status, the Gully Pay invoice that paid for it and the report, under an id that is hard to guess; anyone with the report’s link can read it. To count free checks, re-run credits and duplicates, a check is tied to your workspace when you are signed in, and otherwise to a shortened SHA-256 hash of your IP address. That hash is not salted, so it is pseudonymous: anyone who knows the address can compute it. Your browser remembers the ids of the last 20 checks you started.

Partner launches and webhooks. When a launchpad sends us its new launches with its API key, we keep each launch’s chain, token and transaction, the map’s result, the workspace’s webhook address, its signing secret and its threshold, and a log of deliveries. Badges and the map frame on embed.gullylabs.xyz are drawn from maps we already hold, set no cookies and record nothing about who views them.

Gully Score. Looking up a score needs no account and we don’t record who looked. We keep each contract’s latest score and its history. The contract address is sent to Sourcify, Etherscan and public blockchain nodes to read its evidence. Lookups are limited per IP address in memory only.

sections.h: Billing: Gully Pay and public chains
p: Payments happen on public blockchains. A transaction, the addresses in it and the amount are public and permanent, and nobody (us included) can change or delete them. We never hold your funds.

When you pay us or a Gully Pay store, we record the transaction hash, chain, asset, amount, its US dollar value at the time, the paying address and the block, to confirm and receipt the payment. A store’s owner sees its own payments, and its webhook sends the payment, including the paying address, to the address the store sets. A store can put a customer name and email on an invoice; the store decides that, and is responsible for it. We count how often an invoice page is opened, without storing who opened it.

For a store we keep its name, logo (copied once from the address given, never hot-linked), accent colour, support email, website, receiving wallets, which version of the merchant terms it accepted and with which wallet, its invoices, links, fees and statements.

One cookie of ours: the app’s sign-in cookie (__Host-gl_dev), only after you sign in. It is HttpOnly, sent only to the app over HTTPS, and lasts 30 days or until you sign out. The checkout pages, the API and embed.gullylabs.xyz set no cookies.
No advertising or cross-site tracking cookies, and Gully Analytics uses none.

Browser storage remembers choices on your device only: the app’s sidebar, invites you declined, that you accepted the swap risk notice, recent Gully AI questions in the app, requests you already sent (Chain Kit, devnet waitlist), that you closed the announcement bar or the install card, the Deep checks you started, and chart and tab choices.
